title: Graceful session resumption and tool retry patterns across TS/Python/Go SDKs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce uniform session-resumption and tool-retry semantics in TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs to improve reliability for long-lived streaming invocations (chat/generation) and tool/function calling. This ticket defines patterns, compatibility shims for older clients, examples, and the migration plan for customers relying on progressive JSON events and resumable sessions.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose a session token and resume API for streaming invocations that preserves KV cache offsets and partial tool transcripts
Tool/function calls are retried idempotently using SDK-managed idempotency keys and retry backoff, with developer ability to opt-out per-call
Resumption respects schema constraints: partial structured outputs are merged, and schema validation errors are surfaced to the client in a deterministic way
Compatibility mode: old clients (pre-sdks-2026.01) can still receive non-resumable streams without breakage
End-to-end tests exercising network interruption, server failover, and client upgrade scenarios pass in CI (>=95% pass rate)
implementation_plan: Finalize protocol: event envelope fields for resume_token, seq_offset, kv_snapshot_ref, and partial_schema_patch
Implement core resume token generation on runtime side with signed TTL and variant mapping
TS/Py/Go SDKs: add ResumeSession() + SessionHandle abstraction; implement local KV replay and partial-output rehydration
Add per-call idempotencyKey param and default SDK strategy (UUID v4 + timestamp) for tool invocations
Provide opt-out flag for automatic retries and expose retry metadata to user callbacks
Add schema-aware merge helpers in SDKs: progressiveJson.mergePartial(base, patch) implementations
Add feature flag gating in runtime for gradual rollout (20% -> 60% -> 100%)
Ship experimental docs and example apps (chat-with-tools-resume) for each language
notes: This work is motivated by production incidents where long chats lost context after transient network partitions, causing poor UX and duplicate tool side-effects.
Resumption must not re-run non-idempotent side effects in connected tool endpoints; need explicit at-most-once helpers and clear doc guidance.
Signed resume tokens limit surface area for abuse; token revocation handled by short TTLs and server-side session invalidation endpoints.
risks: Complexity of merging partial structured outputs could lead to silent data loss if schemas evolve incompatibly
Operators may rely on KV cache semantics that differ across model/backends; must document guarantees and limits
Compatibility shim increases runtime code paths; thorough testing required to avoid throughput regressions
open_questions: Should resume tokens be opaque server-signed blobs or structured claims (faster debuggability)?
What's the retention window for resumable sessions by default (1h vs 24h)?
How to surface resumptions in Console observability (trace spans, resume_count metric)?
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with runtime, SDK, and security teams. Agreed to server-signed opaque tokens with HMAC and 1h default TTL.
2026-02-28: PoC TS SDK can resume a streaming invocation on reconnect and replayed KV snapshot. Initial merge helper implemented using deep-merge-with-arrays-by-key.
2026-03-04: Security review flagged token leakage risk in client logs; SDKs now scrub resume_token from default error messages.
2026-03-09: Added idempotencyKey param to tool invocation interfaces in all three PoC branches. Backoff policy: jittered exponential with max 5 retries for idempotent calls.
2026-03-12: Integration smoke tests: simulated network blips show successful resume with consistent generated text and single tool invocation observed by instrumented test tool endpoint.
2026-03-14: Preparing RFC for SDK public API changes and deprecation timeline for old streaming call signatures. Targeting beta release in sdk-2026.03
qa_plan: Unit tests for session handle lifecycle and resume token parsing in TS/Py/Go
Property-based tests for progressiveJson.mergePartial covering common schema evolution cases
Integration tests simulating: client disconnect during streaming, reconnect with different SDK version, server node failover
E2E tests with instrumented tool endpoints to assert at-most-once semantics for non-idempotent tools
Performance benchmark comparing throughput and p99 latency before/after feature flag enabled
migration_notes: Backward compatibility: server will send legacy event format when client declares compatibility header 'X-RW-SDK: legacy'
We will provide a small shim in TS SDK that auto-falls back to legacy streaming for older runtime deployments until rollout completes
Deprecation: old streaming-only endpoints will be announced 6 weeks before removal; provide migration-cli to convert transcripts into resumable session experiments
next_steps: Finish API ergonomics PR for TS SDK and gather feedback from platform and SDK users (due 2026-03-18)
Run larger chaos runs on staging for resume behaviour (target 3/20)
Prepare changelog and migration guide draft for /docs/sdk/resume-and-retries.md
